# Calibrated Agent Evaluation

> Check your LLM judge before you trust its numbers. Error analysis and judge calibration for AI agents: label your agent's traces, name its failure modes, check an LLM judge against your labels, and gate CI only on a judge that passed. It is offline by default and ships as a Python library and CLI with no hosted service.

The toolkit evaluates agents from their traces, so a hand-coded loop, an LLM with MCP tools, a single agent and a crew all reduce to the same `Trace` and one human label. A judge scores only after it agrees with human labels on both failures and passes and after its verdicts hold steady under a bias battery. The CI gate (`run --ci`) passes a failure mode when a cautious lower bound on its pass rate, from the certified judge's verdicts, human labels or code scorers, clears the threshold. Next to the gate, the report gives each judged mode's failure rate with the judge's measured error removed and a 95% range; that corrected rate does not change the exit code, and it is withheld when the judge is too weak, the labels too few, or the rate sample under 150 traces. The base install has one runtime dependency (Pydantic); every capability beyond the offline local backend is an opt-in extra. Distribution name `calibrated-agent-evaluation`, CLI `calibrated-agent-evaluation`, import name `calibrated_agent_evaluation`, license Apache-2.0.

The pipeline is one command per stage, in workflow order: `define → generate → label → cluster → calibrate → bias → judge → run → improve`, with `ingest`, `capture` and `probe` to bring traces in.

## Start here

- [Why check your judge](why/): what goes wrong when a team trusts an unchecked LLM judge, told through public incidents and one support team's agent, plus the cost, when this is overkill, and where it fits beside other tools.
- [Walkthrough](walkthrough/): the whole loop on OrderBot, a sample refund agent, one step per page, each with the CLI and the Claude Code skill.
  - [0. Decide what good means](walkthrough/define/), [1. Make test inputs](walkthrough/generate/), [2. Read and label traces](walkthrough/label/), [3. Name what goes wrong](walkthrough/cluster/), [4. Put a judge on probation](walkthrough/judge/), [5. Gate your pull requests](walkthrough/gate/), [6. Check that a fix worked](walkthrough/improve/), [7. Watch production](walkthrough/production/).

## Connect your agent

- [Connect your agent](integrate/): five ways to get an agent's runs in, chosen with a short decision tree, and what each gives you.
- [Ingest trace files](integrate/ingest-existing-traces/): OpenTelemetry (GenAI, OpenLLMetry, OpenInference), Strands, Inspect, JSONL and parquet traces you already export.
- [Read from Langfuse](integrate/langfuse/): ingest from a Langfuse project, or use Langfuse as the store.
- [Capture in process](integrate/capture-and-ingest/): run your agent once and store the spans it emitted.
- [Route your agent through](integrate/route-your-agent/): let the toolkit drive a Strands topology, an Inspect solver or an AgentCore Runtime over generated inputs, with offline cassette replay.
- [Probe a black-box endpoint](integrate/probe-black-box/): an HTTP or WebSocket endpoint you can only call, or an agent on AgentCore Runtime by its ARN.
- [Bedrock AgentCore](integrate/agentcore/): run, probe, audit A/B tests, publish evaluation datasets and certify online judges for AgentCore, with its troubleshooting.
- [Integration gallery](integrate/gallery/): one recipe per trace source.

## How-to

- [How-to](how-to/): short task pages.
- [Install](how-to/install/): PyPI or a checkout, Python 3.11.5+, and the extras each command needs.
- [Use the Claude Code skills](how-to/claude-code-skills/): the plugin that lets a coding agent run the loop with you.
- [Configure the CI job](how-to/ci-config/): GitHub Actions and GitLab snippets, seeding the job's store, verdict sources, exit codes, drift and publishing.
- [Review traces in the UI](how-to/review-ui/): the keyboard-driven, critique-first labeling app and rater agreement.
- [Evaluate a multi-agent crew](how-to/evaluate-a-crew/): which agent caused a failure versus where it showed up.
- [Rank subjective qualities](how-to/rank-subjective-qualities/): pairwise preferences for qualities with no pass/fail, tracked and never gated.
- [Check for drift](how-to/drift-check/): whether production still looks like the traces the judge was checked on.
- [Write an improve request](how-to/improve-request-file/): check a fix measured outside the toolkit.
- [Run fully offline](how-to/offline/): cassette replay, a judge on your own hardware, and which extras reach the network.
- [Troubleshooting](how-to/troubleshooting/): each message the CLI prints when it can't give an answer, its cause, and what to do.

## Reference

- [CLI](cli/): every `calibrated-agent-evaluation` command and flag.
- [Python API](reference/): the library surface, generated from docstrings.
- [Trace format](trace-format/): the `Trace`, `Span` and `Label` models and the dump format.
- [Bias probe files](bias-probe-format/): the format of a judge's bias battery.
- [Methods and citations](methods/): every statistical method the toolkit ships, its formula, code location and primary source.
- [Reviewer notes](reviewer-notes/): where the corrected-rate interval was measured to cover less often than 95%, and the evidence files.
- [Glossary](glossary/): every term the docs use with a specific meaning.
- [Versioning and stability](versioning/): the current release, the schema version of each persisted record, and the dependency pins.
